oracle_clues: Issue expectation: linspace(X, X, N) should yield N copies of X.
PR summary: for np.linspace(np.inf, np.inf, N), the wrong output is "[nan nan ... nan inf]" and the correct output should be "[inf inf ... inf]".

Implementation note in diff: equal endpoints (including equal infinities) must produce a zero step; prior subtraction inf - inf yields spurious nan and an invalid value warning, which then propagates into the result.

category_specific_evidence: np.linspace(np.inf, np.inf, N) returned [nan nan ... nan inf] instead of [inf inf ... inf] (gh-26699).
Issue reproduction: np.linspace(np.inf, np.inf, 4) emitted RuntimeWarning: "invalid value encountered in subtract" and returned array([nan, nan, nan, inf]).
Root cause: delta = stop - start produced nan via inf - inf, which then propagated through subsequent multiplications; only the last element was rescued by y[-1] = stop assignment.

Fix: equal endpoints (including equal infinities) must produce a zero step, so subtraction is skipped for those elements; this avoids the spurious "invalid value" warning from inf - inf (implemented via equal = start == stop and using where=~equal with out=np.zeros(...)).
Fix detail: "replace any nan in delta with zero wherever start == stop"; also notes "nan == nan is False identity ensures NaN inputs are unaffected in this case".

Correct handling expectation asserted in issue: linspace(X, X, N) should produce N copies of X; for start=stop=+inf and N=4 expected [inf, inf, inf, inf] (no NaNs; step should be zero for equal infinities).

Test added: test_inf_equal_endpoints asserts linspace(inf, inf, num) equals np.full(num, inf) for num in [2, 5, 50] and checks RuntimeWarning is raised as error; also asserts linspace(np.inf, np.inf, 5, endpoint=False) yields all +inf and checks retstep case for y, step = linspace(np.inf, np.inf, 2, retstep=True).
reproduction_risks: Special value handling for equal endpoints: reproduction must use start == stop with infinities (+inf and/or -inf) to hit the inf - inf subtraction path.

Warning checking: fixed behavior should avoid spurious RuntimeWarning "invalid value encountered in subtract"; repro should either observe/allow or assert absence/presence of that warning depending on whether it targets buggy vs fixed behavior.
Endpoint behavior: tests also cover endpoint=False; include this if verifying propagation past endpoint handling, since earlier buggy output depended on y[-1] assignment rescue.
